jobs.excerpt: About HubSync:HubSync is a fast-growing SaaS company revolutionizing how top accounting firms manage their client engagement processes.
jobs.description:
About HubSync:

HubSync is a fast-growing SaaS company revolutionizing how top accounting firms manage their client engagement processes. Our cloud-based platform streamlines workflows and automates complex tasks, empowering firms to deliver exceptional client experiences while increasing efficiency. As we continue to scale, we're looking for passionate team members who thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

About this role

HubSync is hiring a Senior SDET, Framework & Enablement, to own the health of our end-to-end test automation and make it easy for every engineer to contribute tests that meet the standard. Our customers run their busiest weeks of the year on HubSync, and our test pipeline has to be something they can count on: when a pipeline is red, it means something real; when it is green, the team trusts it enough to ship.

Our test framework is AI-assisted by design. Engineers define what a test should check, Claude Code writes the test code under versioned skill-file rules, and a convention linter plus tiered CI gates (PR, deploy, and nightly) hold the standard. The architecture is settled. This person will own it, extend it, and help the rest of engineering use it well. Success is measured by how many people contribute strong tests, not by how many tests this person writes.

Key Responsibilities

Gate & Signal Ownership

  • Triage CI failures to root cause, so every gate failure gets a real disposition instead of a re-run.
  • Run test quarantine with discipline: flaky tests go in with a tracking ticket and an owner, and come back out fixed or deleted.
  • Lead the quarterly review of the PR gate so only tests that earn their place stay in it.
  • Protect signal quality over green builds; a gate that passes because tests were skipped or deleted is a failed gate.

Framework Engineering

  • Own and extend the shared test framework: fixtures, factories, the API client, page object conventions, and CI test mapping.
  • Lead the move of the convention linter from shell-based checks to AST-aware tooling.
  • Build reusable patterns for hard problems, such as complex grid assertions and external signing ceremonies, so feature teams don't have to solve them again.

AI-Assisted Test Development

  • Own the skills system that governs AI-written tests; design the rules that define what the model may write and what it must refuse.
  • Trace violations in AI-written tests back to their source and fix them in the skill files, not in review comments.
  • Re-validate those rules whenever the underlying model changes.
  • Review generated tests for convention compliance and real test value.
  • Help developers adopt the workflow: pair on their first tests, turn recurring friction into framework fixes or skill updates, and keep the path from test idea to merged, passing test short.

Direct Test Authoring

  • Write tests, page objects, and fixtures directly where the stakes or the difficulty call for it: critical-path coverage, reference implementations that set the pattern, and problems too complex to delegate.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years in software development in test, test automation, or developer-tooling roles within a SaaS environment.
  • Proven experience building or owning a test framework, not just writing tests inside one.
  • Hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines, including being the person accountable when the build broke.
  • Deep TypeScript expertise; Playwright strongly preferred.
  • Strong review judgment: the ability to look at a passing test and tell whether it verifies anything.
  • Demonstrated track record of making other engineers more productive through internal tooling, developer experience improvements, or documentation teams rely on.
  • Genuine interest in AI-assisted development and the governance questions that come with it.
  • Experience in tax, accounting, fintech, or another regulated industry is a plus.

What this role is not

  • Not a manual QA or test-execution role.
  • Not a script factory. Test count is not the goal. Making the whole team able to write good tests is.
  • Not a mandate to redesign the framework. The architecture is settled, and this role extends it within established conventions.
  • Not the owner of AI feature quality. Evaluating HubSync's own AI features (evals, rubrics, tracing, adversarial testing) is a separate discipline. This role partners on that work but doesn't own it.

Technologies

TypeScript, Playwright, CI/CD with tiered test gates, AST-based linting, Claude Code with versioned skill files, React and Node.js applications, and AWS.

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

Bonus

jobs.excerpt: DescriptionVi Operate puts AI agents into the daily operations of large health systems, providers, and pharma organizations.
jobs.description:
Description

Vi Operate puts AI agents into the daily operations of large health systems, providers, and pharma organizations. Augment is the voice capability underneath it: the agents that call patients and providers, hold a real conversation, and take action in the systems where the work actually lives. This is a dedicated quality role for that work.

Testing a voice agent is not like testing software that returns the same answer twice. A similar call can go three different ways. A model update can quietly change behavior that nothing in a unit test would catch. When a call goes badly, the cause could be the speech recognition, the model, the voice synthesis, the telephony layer, or the integration underneath, and the transcript alone won't tell you which. Making that testable, repeatable, and catchable before a client hears it is the job.

You will own quality for agents that call real patients, providers, and caregivers. That means building the test and evaluation systems our engineers develop against, deciding what has to pass before something ships, and being the person who can take a bad call recording and say what actually went wrong. We need someone who has done classical QA properly and has since tested voice and LLM systems in production, because this role needs all three.

What You'll Own

  • Voice testing and debugging. Call recordings, transcripts, latency traces, and logs. Isolating which layer failed: speech to text, the model, text to speech, telephony, or the integration behind it. Turning a vague "the call went badly" into a reproducible ticket an engineer can act on.
  • Evaluation and regression testing. Golden test sets, simulated calls, judged transcripts, accuracy on classification and extraction, and structured output validation. Regression coverage that still holds when the underlying model changes.
  • Testing things that aren't deterministic. Deciding what "passing" means when the output varies run to run. Setting tolerances, handling flake honestly rather than by rerunning until green, and keeping the suite trustworthy enough that engineers act on a failure.
  • Release criteria. What has to be true before an agent goes live for a client, and what has to stay true afterward. You set the bar and you hold it, including when a deployment date is pushing on it.
  • Classical QA for the rest of the product. Test plans, regression suites, bug triage, reproductions, and CI integration for everything around the agent.
  • Quality in production. Sampling live calls after release, spotting drift and degradation, and getting it in front of the right engineer before the client raises it.
  • Breaking it on purpose. Red-teaming the agent before someone outside does. Prompt injection through the documents it reads, callers who talk it off script or push it toward giving medical advice, people claiming to be someone they aren't to get patient information out of it. You test that the guardrails and access controls actually hold under pressure, not just that they exist.

What We're Looking For

  • QA on production voice agents. You have tested a system that talks to people on the phone, and you can walk through a real failure you diagnosed: what you heard, where you looked, and which layer turned out to be at fault. This is required and it's what we screen hardest on.
  • QA on LLM systems. You have tested something built on a language model in production, not as a side project, and you can describe how you decided whether it was working.
  • Real classical QA depth. Test strategy, test planning, regression suites, bug triage, and release process. You have worked somewhere QA had teeth.
  • Testing non-deterministic systems. You have dealt with output that varies and made it testable anyway, and you can explain the tradeoffs you made to get there.
  • Python and test automation. You write your own tooling and wire it into CI rather than filing a ticket for someone else to.
  • Judgment about severity. You can tell the difference between a cosmetic defect and something that will mislead a patient on a phone call, and you can defend that call to an engineer who disagrees.
  • A system mindset. You look at the whole system rather than one piece, and your first instinct is to find where it comes apart. You think about the seams between components, the inputs nobody planned for, and the person on the other end trying to get something out of it that they shouldn't.

Nice To Have

  • Background in IVR, contact center, or CCaaS quality (Genesys, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect, Twilio, or similar)
  • Audio and network condition testing: codecs, jitter, packet loss, barge-in and interruption handling
  • Familiarity with evaluation tooling such as LLM-as-judge harnesses, prompt regression frameworks, or simulated conversation testing
  • Healthcare or pharma experience, and comfort working under HIPAA
  • Experience standing up a QA function rather than joining one
  • Load and performance testing on real-time systems
  • Spanish proficiency, enough to listen to a call and judge whether the agent handled it

Job Description

This position is a fully remote role and requires working hours in EST or CST. An active and clear RN and APRN or Physician Assistant license in GA, PA, and/or OH is required at time of hire.

A bit about this role:

The Gold Care Program is a highly collaborative, multidisciplinary team of physicians, advanced practice providers, nurse case managers, social work case managers, community health workers, and scheduling team, united by our mission to build a better care delivery system for Devoted’s most complex members. We provide whole-person clinical, social and logistical support for patients with complex chronic conditions, frail elders, and patients at high risk of hospital admissions.

The Advanced Practice Provider (APP) role on the Gold Care team is to reinforce and adjust the patient’s plan of care according to what matters most to the patient, their clinical picture, and in response to any barriers or obstacles they are facing. They manage the clinical trajectory of the patient including symptom management, chronic disease management, and adjustments to the clinical plan. The NP’s clinical decision making and bias-to-action ensures we continuously deliver on meeting patients’ needs as determined by both the interdisciplinary team and by the patient’s priorities.

Responsibilities and Impact will include:

  • Deliver exceptional care to a cohort of complex patients across multiple geographies, leveraging video telehealth visits and an interdisciplinary team.

  • Guide and oversee the medical management of patients (utilizing the 5M framework) during their tenure with Gold Care.

  • Work closely with other members of the patient's care team including their PCP, specialists, and other Devoted teams such as pharmacy, or specialty care. You will also collaborate with the patients’ support systems such as family members and caregivers in order to coordinate care for the patient and deliver a collaborative care plan.

  • For patients in Gold Care, perform comprehensive assessment visits, provide post-acute transition support, comprehensive diagnosis/disease review, medication review, and assessment for quality of care (Stars/Hedis) interventions as well as social and home health/DME needs.

  • In infrequent instances when appropriate and compliant with NP licensure, you may also provide telehealth visits to members outside of your panel to support other Devoted Medical service lines

  • As the program continues to grow, there may be an infrequent weekend on-call component to support our clinical nurses who triage calls from our members during the weekend.

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient medical records, ensuring compliance with relevant legal and ethical guidelines.

  • Adhere to all relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards, including patient privacy and telehealth regulations.

  • Experience working in a fast-paced, high-energy organization

Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Aperçu de l’entreprise

Chez Motorola Solutions, nous pensons que tout commence par nos employés. Nous sommes une communauté mondiale soudée, unie par la volonté incessante de contribuer à la sécurité des personnes partout dans le monde. Nous concevons et connectons des technologies qui contribuent à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures. Nos solutions favorisent la collaboration essentielle pour améliorer la sécurité des populations, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des entreprises et, finalement, des nations. Connectez-vous à une carrière qui compte et aidez-nous à bâtir un avenir plus sûr.


Department Overview

Hyper, a Motorola Solutions Company, is a leader in conversational, agentic AI designed to reduce the burden on understaffed public safety answering points (PSAPs) by handling non-emergency calls. It is revolutionizing emergency response systems through cutting-edge AI technologies. Our first product is reducing 911 wait times by alleviating administrative work from highly trained 911 telecommunicators.


Job Description

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join the AI Agent Platform team behind Hyper’s emergency response products (Motorola Solutions announced that it acquired Hyper on April 9, 2026).


You’ll work alongside experienced engineers across real-time AI pipelines, telephony, backend infrastructure, and product surfaces. You’ll help influence architecture, build core product features, and shape how our team uses AI agents to move faster without compromising reliability, security, or product quality. We encourage engineers to use AI agents in their own work. But because this is mission-critical software, humans still own quality, judgment, and what ships.

What You’ll Do

  • Build real-time voice AI features for emergency response workflows.
  • Design and operate LLM-powered systems that support human 911 telecommunicators.
  • Own features across the stack, from backend services and AI pipelines to frontend interfaces and internal tools.
  • Work on low-latency audio processing, streaming systems, telephony integrations, and human-in-the-loop AI workflows.
  • Help integrate speech models, LLMs, and emerging AI technologies into production systems.
  • Build strong habits around tests, code review, observability, and security from day one.
  • Help write and improve evaluation, testing, and observability for AI-assisted systems.
  • Participate in on-call responsibilities (with support and shadow rotations to start), backed by clear runbooks and blameless post-incident reviews.
  • Ask questions, dig into how things work, and bring fresh perspectives to the team.

You Might Be a Fit If

  • You’re curious about working across backend, infrastructure, AI, and product, even if you haven’t done it all yet.
  • You use AI tools daily, but you do not confuse speed with quality.
  • You care about quality — you write tests, read documentation, and try to understand a system before you change it.
  • You take feedback well and act on it.
  • You have strong product instincts and care about the humans using what you build.
  • You thrive in a small, fast-moving team where you’ll have real ownership early — and you’re comfortable asking for help.
  • You want to work on AI systems that matter beyond demos.

Relevant Experience

We don’t expect you to have shipped production systems. We care most about engineering fundamentals, learning velocity, curiosity, and how you think. Coursework, internships, research, and personal projects all count.

Relevant exposure may include:

  • Projects involving LLMs, AI agents, AI pipelines, RAG systems, evals, or prompt test harnesses.
  • Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, Voice Activity Detection, endpointing, interruption handling, noise filtering, diarization, or audio streaming.
  • Telephony and voice infrastructure, including PSTN, SIP trunking, PBX, and call routing.
  • Real-time communication systems using WebRTC, WebSockets, RTP/SRTP, media streaming, or low-latency audio transport.
  • Programming in Elixir, Go, Python, Rust, or similar languages.
  • Familiarity with PostgreSQL or relational data modeling.
  • Exposure to cloud infrastructure on AWS, Azure, or GCP
  • Docker, Kubernetes, or similar deployment environments.
  • Internships or co-ops in software engineering, infrastructure, or AI/ML roles.

You do not need experience in all of these areas. Most successful candidates will have experience in a few and curiosity to learn the rest

These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Denmark Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-120,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

Who We Are:

Headquartered in Washington, DC, Versar Global Solutions provides full mission lifecycle solutions for challenges faced by our government and commercial Customers in the natural, built, and digital environments. With team members around the world and a rich legacy spanning more than 50 years, Versar Global Solutions delivers a broad array of planning, analysis and risk management solutions, project and program management, operations and maintenance services, and information technology applications for environmental management and remediation projects, mission critical facilities and installations, and in support of readiness and contingency operations.

Who You Are:

You are a strategic, client-focused leader with deep experience in environmental remediation, environmental health, and federal environmental program delivery. You combine technical credibility, business leadership, and disciplined execution to help federal customers investigate, manage, remediate, and close contaminated sites while protecting workers, communities, ecological receptors, and mission operations. You build high-performing multidisciplinary teams, strengthen technical standards, grow client relationships, and translate regulatory, scientific, safety, and stakeholder requirements into practical, defensible, and executable solutions.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and grow Versar’s Integrated Planning & Permitting service line in support of U.S. federal customers, establishing strategic priorities, annual operating objectives, technical standards, and measurable performance goals.
  • Develop and execute a service line growth strategy that integrates National Environmental Policy Act compliance, installation and master planning, area development planning, natural and cultural resources, environmental permitting, stakeholder engagement, and related advisory services.
  • Serve as a senior client and technical advisor, helping federal agencies define planning and permitting strategies that align mission requirements, infrastructure investments, environmental stewardship, schedules, budgets, and implementation constraints.
  • Oversee delivery of complex programs and projects involving NEPA documentation, master plans, installation development plans, area development plans, planning studies, site-selection analyses, environmental baseline studies, and implementation roadmaps.
  • Guide multidisciplinary teams in integrating land use, facilities, infrastructure, transportation, utilities, resilience, sustainability, encroachment, natural resources, cultural resources, and environmental compliance considerations into defensible planning decisions.
  • Provide senior oversight for environmental permitting and consultation strategies, including requirements associated with wetlands and waters, threatened and endangered species, historic properties, air quality, water quality, stormwater, coastal resources, hazardous materials, and other applicable federal, state, tribal, and local approvals.
  • Establish project governance, quality-management, and technical-review processes that produce accurate, consistent, auditable, and implementation-ready deliverables.
  • Advise project teams on purpose and need, alternatives development, cumulative effects, mitigation, agency coordination, consultation, public involvement, permit sequencing, regulatory risk, and administrative-record considerations.
  • Build, mentor, and retain a multidisciplinary team of planners, NEPA practitioners, permitting specialists, natural and cultural resource professionals, engineers, scientists, GIS analysts, technical editors, and project managers.
  • Plan workforce capacity, identify critical skill gaps, support recruiting and professional development, and coordinate resources across offices, business areas, and partner organizations.
  • Maintain trusted relationships with federal program executives, contracting personnel, installation leaders, regulators, resource agencies, tribal representatives, team partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Champion innovation and technology-enabled delivery by identifying, evaluating, piloting, and scaling practical solutions that enhance technical quality, data integrity, decision-making, project efficiency, lifecycle cost, and environmental outcomes.
  • Lead capture and proposal activities for strategic federal opportunities, including market positioning, client engagement, solution development, teaming, technical approaches, staffing plans, basis of estimate, risk reviews, and oral presentations.
  • Monitor market, policy, regulatory, funding, and acquisition developments affecting federal integrated planning and permitting services and translating them into service offerings and investment priorities.
  • Oversee service line financial and operational performance, including pipeline, backlog, revenue, profitability, utilization, project health, forecast accuracy, and corrective actions, consistent with assigned authority and company procedures.
  • Partner with business development, operations, contracts, finance, legal, health and safety, quality, and other corporate functions to manage risk and support compliant execution.
  • Represent Versar at client meetings, industry events, professional associations, technical forums, and conferences and strengthen the company’s reputation in federal planning and environmental compliance markets.
  • Perform periodic travel to federal facilities, installations, project sites, client offices, and industry events while complying with applicable safety, security, ethics, and information-handling requirements.
  • What You’ll Bring:
  • Bachelor’s degree in planning, environmental science, natural or cultural resource management, architecture, landscape architecture, engineering, geography, public policy, or related discipline.
  • Twelve or more years of progressively responsible experience in federal planning, NEPA, environmental compliance, permitting, natural resources, cultural resources, or related consulting services, including leadership of complex multidisciplinary programs or portfolios. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting U.S. federal civilian agencies, military departments, federal installations, infrastructure programs, or other mission-oriented federal organizations.
  • Deep working knowledge of NEPA and experience integrating environmental review with master planning, installation planning, area development planning, capital programming, design, construction, or operational decision making.
  • Demonstrated understanding of planning principles and products, including existing-conditions analysis, requirements development, land-use planning, alternatives evaluation, site planning, infrastructure assessment, implementation planning, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Working knowledge of natural and cultural resource requirements and associated agency coordination and consultation processes.
  • Broad knowledge of environmental compliance and permitting requirements applicable to federal facilities, infrastructure, and land-management actions, with the judgment to engage appropriate legal and technical specialists.
  • Experience developing coordinated permitting strategies, approval schedules, compliance matrices, risk registers, mitigation commitments, and implementation roadmaps.
  • Demonstrated success leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, managing managers and technical leads, balancing workload, and maintaining high standards for quality and client service.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify, evaluate, implement, and scale innovative technologies, digital solutions, or improved delivery methods within environmental, engineering, scientific, or federal program environments.
  • Experience managing program or portfolio scope, schedule, budget, staffing, subcontractors, financial performance, quality, and risk across multiple concurrent projects.
  • Demonstrated success with federal business development, capture planning, proposal leadership, client engagement, teaming, and expansion of existing accounts or service offerings.
  • Ability to translate complex planning, regulatory, technical, and stakeholder issues into clear executive decisions, practical delivery strategies, and concise written and visual communications.
  • Exceptional leadership, collaboration, negotiation, facilitation, technical writing, and presentation skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications. Familiarity with geographic information systems, planning and design applications, environmental data systems, project controls, customer relationship management, and business intelligence tools is preferred.
  • Advanced degree, professional planning credential, project management certification, or other relevant professional registration or certification is preferred.
  • Ability to travel to federal customer sites and work in office, field, public-meeting, construction, industrial, or installation environments as required by the assignment.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain the federal background investigation, credential, site access, or security clearance required by the customer or contract.
  • Must be proficient in English, both written and verbal, to ensure effective communication and collaboration.

jobs.description:
Our Security and IT team keeps the 360Learning platform secure, compliant and auditable for the 1,500 organisations that learn on it every day. As a Senior DevSecOps Engineer, your mission is to make our infrastructure secure by design, detectable by default, and provable at audit time.

360Learning runs its learning platform on Azure and Kubernetes, certified ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II. Over the past two years the technical security workload has grown on every front: a larger and more regulated customer base sending their own scans and security assessments, a wider detection and response scope, more infrastructure to keep hardened and auditable, and a growing backlog of security engineering projects that never reach the top of the queue.

We are creating this position to add real technical capacity on the infrastructure side of security, and to move part of our security posture from manual effort to automated guardrails. You will be the bridge between security and platform engineering: deep enough in infrastructure to fix things yourself, and close enough to security operations to know what to look for.

“Ours is a small, senior team with a broad scope: information security, compliance, infrastructure governance and internal tooling, with dual audit accountability on ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II. That means direct impact and no layers between you and the decision. Roughly half of this role is greenfield build work you will own end to end.” Guillaume Seigneuret, CISO and Hiring Coach.

Within 1 month, you will:

    • Complete our onboarding and learn how we work through our own platform and our Convexity culture

    • Map our Azure and AKS environment, our detection and logging coverage, and our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 control scope with the CISO and the Security Engineer

    • Meet the DevOps, platform engineering and IT teams you will work with daily

    • Shadow alert triage and one customer security assessment end to end

Within 3 months, you will:

    • Be autonomous on our AKS and Azure environment and handle infrastructure related alerts end to end

    • Have shipped at least one concrete hardening or automation improvement in production

    • Own the infrastructure scope of vulnerability management, from triage to remediation follow up

Within 6 months, you will:

    • Have the honeypot live and producing high fidelity alerts

    • Have measurably widened SIEM connector coverage, with documented log sources and retention

    • Run infrastructure vulnerability remediation on a predictable cycle with SLA reporting

Within 12 months, you will:

    • Manage detection content as code, with reviewed and tested rules and documented runbooks

    • Have largely automated audit evidence on the infrastructure scope

    • Have eliminated long lived credentials on the critical paths, so engineering teams ship on secure defaults they did not have to think about

The Skill Set:

    • 5+ years in infrastructure, cloud or platform engineering with a strong security focus, or in security engineering with hands on infrastructure practice

    • Production experience with Kubernetes: RBAC, network policies, admission controllers, secrets handling, workload identity, runtime security

    • Solid cloud experience, ideally Azure. Strong AWS or Google Cloud experience with a genuine interest in converting works too

    • Infrastructure as code: Terraform, GitOps workflows, CI/CD pipelines

    • Scripting and automation: Python or Go, plus shell. Comfortable reading and writing code, and opening pull requests on repositories owned by other teams

    • Log analysis and investigation: cloud audit logs, query languages, correlation across identity, network and application sources

    • Fluent English (US/UK) / B2 level or equivalent (FR).

    • Enthusiasm for our working environment explained here:

What we offer:

    • Compensation: Package includes base salary, a variable component and equity 📈

    • Benefits/Perks: Work From Home stipend, RTT, lunch vouchers, medical insurance, gym subscription, 1 month parental leave for the second parent.

    • Balance: Flexible hours, full remote work possible anywhere in France 🏠

    • Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: We have 6 active ERGs including Mental Health, Environmental/Sustainability, Women, Parents, LGBTQIA2S+, and Ethnic Diversity.Each group has at least one executive team member serving as a member of the group, bringing greater awareness to each group’s activities and providing a quick path to impact 🤝

    • Corporate Social Responsibility: Review our CSR Charter: 360learning.com/blog/corporate-social-responsibility-charter 🌎🌏🌍

    • Culture: A framework that will help you make an impact - envision our way of working and our Convexity Culture: & find out more about the teams, product and processes 🚀👩🏻‍💻🏆

Interview Process:

  • Phone Screen with our Talent Acquisition Manager
  • Discovery Meeting with our Head of Security
  • Live exercise with our Head of Security and our Head of Devops: investigation of an incident scenario, or review of an insecure infrastructure configuration
  • Clarification Meeting with the Security Engineer and a DevOps engineer
  • Culture Fit Meeting with our VP of Engineering
  • Offer!

Who We Are

360Learning enables companies to upskill from within by turning their experts into champions for employee, customer, and partner growth. With our LMS for collaborative learning, Learning & Development teams can accelerate upskilling with the help of internal experts instead of slow top-down training. 360Learning is the easiest way to onboard and upskill employees, train customer-facing teams, and enable customers and partners–all from one place.
360Learning powers the future of work at 1,700 organizations. Founded in 2013, 360Learning has raised $240 million with 400+ team members across North America and EMEA.

In concert with our culture, 360Learning believes learning includes everyone and that means embracing the strengths of diversity, connectedness, and inclusion. jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Job Description

PerkinElmer is seeking a Regional Product Manager to serve as an embedded field specialist supporting the commercial organisation in an assigned region. This is a bridge role — sitting between central product management and the regional sales and marketing teams — providing the product expertise, competitive response capability, and local market intelligence that the field organisation needs to win in customer-facing situations.

The Regional PM is the product line's voice in the field. They are the person a regional sales manager calls when a deal requires deep product knowledge, when a competitor launches a new instrument, or when a key customer wants to understand how the product line meets their specific application needs. They bring the centre's strategic thinking to the region, and the region's market reality back to central product management.

Field Commercial Support

  • Provide real-time product expertise to the regional sales team — answering technical and commercial questions, supporting customer demonstrations, and participating in key account meetings where product management presence creates commercial advantage
  • Lead regional competitive response: providing timely, accurate, and commercially useful guidance to the sales team when a competitor launches a new instrument, adjusts pricing, or makes a specific claim in a customer situation
  • Support regional sales management with product mix analysis, product line forecasting inputs, and portfolio utilisation data that helps the region prioritise selling effort
  • Participate in distributor management where the product line is sold through channel partners — providing product training, commercial support, and competitive tools

Launch Localisation & Execution

  • Lead the regional execution of global product launches — adapting central launch plans to regional market conditions, regulatory requirements, and commercial priorities
  • Coordinate with Regional Marketing Managers to ensure launch campaigns, customer events, and demand generation activities reflect the product line's commercial priorities in the region
  • Manage regional beta programmes in partnership with the NPI PM — identifying and engaging appropriate regional beta sites, managing relationships, and ensuring feedback is captured and reported to the central programme team
  • Deliver regional sales training on new product launches — ensuring field commercial teams can demonstrate, position, and close against competitive alternatives from day one of launch

Market Intelligence & Feedback

  • Serve as the regional intelligence feed to central product management — systematically reporting competitive activity, customer feedback, application trends, and market developments that are visible in the field but not from the centre
  • Conduct a minimum of 20 in-depth customer conversations per year specifically focused on market intelligence: competitive usage patterns, unmet application needs, pricing sensitivity, and regional regulatory trends
  • Attend and represent PerkinElmer at regional scientific conferences, trade shows, and customer events — gathering competitive intelligence and building relationships with key opinion leaders in the region

Customer & Stakeholder Relationships

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Broad working knowledge of at least one product line technology (atomic spectroscopy, chromatography, materials characterisation) and its key regional application markets
  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively as a field-based specialist — managing multiple concurrent customer and commercial priorities, often with limited day-to-day management oversight
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills — able to engage credibly with regional sales teams, distributors, and customers across varying technical and commercial contexts
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively within the assigned region (40–50%)

Preferred

  • Advanced degree (MSc, PhD) in a relevant analytical or materials science discipline

  • Prior experience in a field-based role (applications scientist, field sales specialist, or field marketing) that required operating across multiple customer sites and managing competing priorities without close supervision
  • Native or near-native fluency in the primary commercial language of the assigned region (where English is not the dominant commercial language)

jobs.description:
About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.


About This Role

This business- and technically accountable ownership role will focus on transforming the contact center into an agentic, Salesforce-native operating model.


As a SAFe Business Owner, you hold primary accountability for ROI, solution fit, governance, and compliance for the contact center value stream. You define what needs to be built and why, make trade-off decisions across AI agents, human agents, channels, and integrations, and ensure delivery teams deliver outcomes—not just features.


You will lead the shift from a traditional, human-centric service model to an agentic contact center on the Salesforce stack—where AI agents resolve work autonomously, escalate cleanly to humans with full context, and continuously improve using CRM + interaction data. Success is measured in containment, cost-to-serve, CSAT/NPS, FCR, AHT, and sustained adoption—not project on-time delivery alone.


Key Responsibilities / What You Own:

Agentic Contact Center Strategy & Outcomes

  • Own the multi-year vision and value case for an agentic contact center on Salesforce (Agentforce / Agentforce Contact Center, Service Cloud, Omni-Channel, Knowledge, Data Cloud as applicable).
  • Define target operating model: AI-first resolution, human-in-the-loop escalation, supervisor visibility, and continuous learning loops.
  • Work with Contact Center Leadership to set and deploy KPIs (containment / deflection, AHT, FCR, CSAT, backlog, SLA, cost-per-contact) and the roadmap that moves them.

Salesforce Service & Platform Steward

  • Serve as the business/technical bridge for Salesforce Service capabilities supporting contact center transformation, including:
    • Service Cloud case management, Omni-Channel routing/skills/queues
    • Knowledge, macros, workflows/Flows, Service Console experience
    • Voice / CTI patterns (Service Cloud Voice, Agentforce Voice, or telephony partner integrations such as Amazon Connect, Genesys, Five9, etc.)
    • Agentforce Service Agents / agentic orchestration (topics, actions, grounding, guardrails, escalation)
    • Data Cloud / CRM context used to power personalization and agent decisions
  • Translate service operations needs into solution designs that prefer Salesforce OOTB and platform-native patterns before custom build.
  • Partner with Solution Architects, Platform Admins, Developers, Data, Security, and vendors to validate designs, PoCs, and production readiness—while retaining ownership of business intent and acceptance of the solution.
  • Ensure integrations (e.g., SAP order/billing/status, identity, telephony, knowledge sources, analytics) are designed for agentic workflows—not only human screen-pop use cases.

Product Backlog, Prioritization & Value Delivery

  • Own the contact center transformation backlog at the epic/feature level: prioritize for measurable service outcomes, not request volume.
  • Define clear problem statements, solution hypotheses, acceptance criteria, and definition of done for agentic use cases (e.g., order status, returns, appointment setting, billing inquiries, warranty, technical triage).
  • Sequence capability releases: channel by channel / intent by intent—from assisted AI → autonomous containment with safe escalation.
  • Reject or reshape requests that are pure process workarounds, low-ROI customizations, or misaligned with the Salesforce target architecture.

Operating Model, Governance & Adoption

  • Establish governance for AI agents: topic ownership, action inventory, grounding/data access, Trust Layer / responsible AI controls, escalation rules, auditability, and human override.
  • Partner with contact center operations, WFM, QA, training, and knowledge teams to redesign processes, scripts, QA scorecards, and coaching for AI + human collaboration.
  • Drive change management focused on behavior and metric change (how supervisors and agents work), not tool rollout alone.
  • Ensure compliance with enterprise architecture, security, privacy, SDLC, and SAFe / Agile delivery practices.

Required Qualifications:

  • 5+ years in customer service / contact center digital platforms.
  • 5+ years hands-on Salesforce Service Cloud in enterprise environments.
  • Bachelor’s degree.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated ownership of contact center technology transformation involving CRM + omnichannel + voice/digital channels (not just CRM case management enhancements).
  • Practical experience designing or deploying AI-assisted or agentic service (Agentforce, Einstein bots / generative service, conversational AI, intelligent routing, or comparable enterprise agent platforms).
  • Working fluency with Salesforce service architecture concepts: Omni-Channel, Flows, Knowledge, entitlement/case lifecycle, CTI/voice integration patterns, Experience Cloud / self-service (as relevant), and data/integration implications.
  • Ability to evaluate build-vs-configure decisions, identify Salesforce OOTB fit vs. customization risk, and partner credibly with architects and engineers.
  • Experience defining reporting/data requirements for contact center KPIs and using operational data to prioritize backlog (containment, AHT, FCR, CSAT, etc.).
  • Familiarity with ERP/service process integrations (e.g., SAP order-to-cash / billing / status) sufficient to design end-to-end agentic journeys—not as a primary SAP functional consultant.

SAFe Business Owner / Product Leadership

  • Experience acting as (or equivalent to) a SAFe Business Owner, Product Manager, or Digital Product Owner for a complex value stream—accountable for ROI and solution outcomes, not only coordination.
  • Comfortable leading PI Planning participation, prioritizing Features/Epics, accepting increments, and making risk/trade-off decisions live with delivery teams.
  • Strong stakeholder leadership across Operations, IT, Architecture, Data, Security, and vendors—through influence and decision quality, not project control.

Contact Center Domain

  • Deep understanding of omnichannel service (voice, chat, email, messaging, self-service), workforce realities, escalation design, and QA/coaching impacts of automation.
  • Proven ability to redesign service processes for automation-first resolution with safe human handoff.
  • Hands-on experience with Agentforce, Agentforce Contact Center / Voice, Service Cloud Voice, or equivalent CCaaS + CRM unification programs.
  • Salesforce certifications (Service Cloud Consultant, Administrator, AI Associate / Agentforce-related credentials) or equivalent demonstrable platform depth.
  • Experience with Data Cloud, Prompt Builder, Einstein Trust Layer, or LLM grounding/guardrail patterns in production.
  • Prior migration from legacy ACD/CCaaS or fragmented bot stacks onto Salesforce-centric service architecture.
  • SAFe certification (SAFe Agilist / POPM) or demonstrated ART Business Owner experience.
  • HVAC, manufacturing, distribution, or complex B2B/B2C service domain experience a plus.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Operations, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degree in platform and domain depth outweigh credentials.

Pay Range

Factors which may affect pay within this range include, but are not limited to, skills, education, experience, and other unique qualifications of the successful candidate. The pay range will not be below the minimum wage applicable to the jurisdiction in which the applicant is to be employed.

Other Compensation

This position is entitled to short-term cash incentives, subject to plan requirements.

Benefits

Employees are eligible for benefits, including:

Description:

SPS Commerce is a leading provider of cloud-based supply chain management solutions, serving a global network of retail trading partners. We foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment where innovation and continuous improvement are highly valued. Join SPS Commerce and be part of a dynamic team that's transforming the global retail supply chain!

Position Summary:

Buyers find and evaluate SPS Commerce across a growing set of surfaces: paid search and social, Google, AI answer engines, Reddit, G2, and YouTube. No single person owns visibility across all of them today. This role will.

The Senior Digital Marketing Manager owns the paid and organic channels that carry a buyer from first discovery to qualified lead, helping set the strategy, controlling the budget, deciding how we work with agencies, and carrying the number. This is a senior individual contributor role that leads through agencies and cross-functional teams rather than direct reports, reporting to the Director of Digital Marketing.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Paid media: Lead paid media programs across paid search, paid social, display and retargeting, and emerging channels, owning the channel mix and CAC and delivering a measurable improvement in cost per qualified pipeline dollar.
  • Budget management: Manage the full budget cycle: forecasting, pacing, in-quarter reallocation, and the business case for increases, with a clear view of the marginal return of the next dollar in every channel.
  • Experimentation: Run an always-on testing program across creative, audience, offer, bid strategy, and landing-page experience, with clear criteria for what gets cut and what gets scaled.
  • Conversion optimization: Own the paid conversion path from ad to landing page to form, working with web and lifecycle teams to close the gaps that cost conversion.
  • Agency & vendor management: Direct paid agencies and channel reps to outcomes rather than deliverables, and recommend what is worth bringing in-house.
  • Measurement & reporting: Build the measurement layer, including attribution, incrementality testing, and channel-level reporting that connects spend to MQLs, pipeline, and CAC efficiency, and one integrated view of paid and organic performance.
  • Organic growth: Lead the organic growth strategy, roadmap, and OKRs, growing qualified organic traffic and improving conversion from organic visitors to activated users and pipeline.
  • AI visibility (AEO/GEO): Build the SPS AEO/GEO playbook, including citation strategy, content structured for model retrieval, and tracking of SPS share of voice in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI Overviews.
  • Technical SEO oversight: Set technical SEO priorities and hold the agency or specialist accountable for delivery, judging the quality of the work and what is worth engineering time.
  • Community & review presence: Unify SPS presence across Reddit, G2, YouTube, and other community and review surfaces into one discoverability strategy.

Required Qualifications:

  • Experience: 5–7+ years in digital marketing, demand generation, or growth at a B2B SaaS, fintech, or technology company, including direct ownership of a paid media budget and an organic search program.
  • Paid media depth: Hands-on command of paid search and paid social, including owning a meaningful budget, building a channel mix from scratch, and defending where every dollar went and what it returned.
  • Pipeline and budget orientation: Thinks in SQLs, pipeline, CAC, and payback, not impressions and rankings. Able to build the business case for more spend and to recognize when to hand budget back.
  • AI visibility fluency: Active experimentation with citation strategies, structured content for model consumption, or measuring share of voice in answer engines. This cannot be trained on the job.
  • Technical SEO literacy: Understanding of site architecture, schema, crawl, and Core Web Vitals sufficient to set priorities, brief a specialist or agency, and tell strong work from weak. Hands-on technical expertise is not required.
  • Content instincts: Ability to distinguish content that earns trust from content that fills a page, with experience working alongside content teams operating at scale.
  • Vendor management: Experience managing agencies and holding them to outcomes, not just deliverables, and judgment on when to stop outsourcing and bring work in-house.
  • Measurement rigor: Comfort with the limits of attribution and the ability to design tests that produce a defensible read anyway.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: Makes consequential decisions with incomplete data and prefers building a function from scratch over running one that is already humming.
  • Experimentation mindset: Treats failure as a feedback loop, running experiments, cutting what does not work quickly, and doubling down on what does.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience navigating a major Google algorithm update that materially impacted the business, including diagnosing, adapting, and recovering.
  • Experience running incrementality or geo-holdout testing on paid channels and changing a budget decision based on the results.
  • Understanding of how retrieval-augmented generation systems select and rank sources, and the ability to translate that into actionable content and structural strategy.
  • Hands-on use of AI and automation tools in day-to-day workflows.
  • Experience in a regulated or compliance-sensitive industry.

Location:

This role is open to fully remote candidates in the United States and Canada, with hybrid options available at our Minneapolis, MN; Toronto, ON; and Rogers, AR offices.


What We Offer:

At SPS Commerce, we are committed to ensuring that each employee’s compensation reflects their unique experiences, performance, and skills in their role. The salary range for this role considers several factors, including education, relevant skills, work history, certifications, location, and more.

The annual salary range for this role is: US Remote, $76,700.00–$118,900.00; Canada Remote, $87,200.00–$130,800.00 CAD. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the factors listed above and may fall anywhere within the range.

Additionally, you may also be eligible to participate in an annual incentive program. An incentive award, if granted, is based on individual and/or organizational performance.

At SPS we power connections that drive the world of commerce forward, and our success depends on making strong decisions, fostering innovation, delivering unparalleled customer solutions, and driving outstanding business performance. We achieve this by creating an environment where every employee feels a true sense of belonging. We embrace diversity, equity, and inclusion, ensuring everyone feels accepted, valued, and empowered to make a meaningful impact.

The Zillow Group Legal and Compliance Department is a dedicated team of skilled (and fun!) legal professionals who enjoy working in a collegial environment within an innovative, fast-paced tech, real estate, and media company. This role is part of the Business Lines Legal Team, which provides frontline legal support for Zillow's products and services, including Zillow Home Loans and our integrated mortgage and real estate offerings.

About the role

We are looking for a talented attorney to serve as dedicated product counsel for Zillow Home Loans (ZHL) mortgage products. This role sits at the intersection of regulated consumer lending and product development, and is well suited for a lawyer energized by translating complex mortgage regulation into clear, practical guidance that helps product teams build and ship.

You will be the day-to-day legal partner to the product and engineering teams building mortgage and integrated home-buying experiences, from affordability and pre-approval tools to AI-powered and agentic features and internal systems for ZHL's own loan officers. You will own the full legal lifecycle across the product portfolio, advise directly on complex and first-of-kind product questions, and work closely with specialized Legal and Compliance teams to support product development and launch. You will also coordinate with legal leadership on matters that present enterprise-level or cross-business-line risk.

The right candidate has solid grounding in the mortgage regulatory framework, is comfortable getting hands-on with AI-enabled product features, has strong drafting, negotiation and communication skills, and the desire to grow subject matter expertise in a domain where product scope evolves and regulatory expectations shift. You are pragmatic, responsive, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating autonomously within a defined scope.

In this role, you will get to:

  • Serve as the primary day-to-day legal point of contact for an assigned set of ZHL mortgage products, providing full lifecycle counsel from concept and design through launch and iteration
  • Advise product and engineering teams on the state and federal mortgage regulatory framework, including RESPA, TILA , ECOA, UDAAP, and state mortgage licensing
  • Partner directly with AI/ML engineering teams on compliance guardrails for AI-enabled and agentic product features, including hands-on testing of model outputs and development of evaluation criteria for legal and regulatory compliance
  • Provide practical, risk-calibrated guidance on product design and disclosures, including how and where mortgage content, pre-approval, and loan application experiences are surfaced across ZHL's platforms
  • Embed with business partners on issues of first impression, pilot programs, and other key initiatives, delivering legal risk analysis and recommendations directly to senior management
  • Draft, review, and negotiate the commercial and data-rights agreements that support your products, such as vendor, technology, and services agreements

Who you are

You are a responsive, pragmatic, and detail-oriented attorney who has:

  • Substantive command of the mortgage and consumer lending regulatory framework, with the depth to advise directly on the statutes above as they apply to live product decisions

The DevSecOps Engineer will also mentor team members on secure coding and infrastructure practices, leading cross-functional alignment between engineering, security, and operations teams.


Responsibilities:

- Lead the design, implementation, and maintenance of secure CI/CD pipelines, automating security scanning (SAST, DAST, SCA) alongside build, test, and deployment processes.

- Implement and manage container security and orchestration technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) to optimize deployment and runtime safety.


- Stay up to date with emerging industry trends, security standards, and best practices in DevSecOps, cloud security, and vulnerability management.


- Provide guidance, training, and mentorship to team members on secure development lifecycle (SDLC) practices and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) security.
