    • Own relationships with OpenAI, Anthropic, and other relevant enterprise AI technology providers.
    • Evaluate new platform capabilities and determine when they should be enabled, restricted, piloted, or adopted broadly.
    • Ensure enterprise AI tools align with Sedgwick's broader AI architecture and do not create unmanaged technology or data silos.
    • Establish operational dashboards for adoption, usage, cost, risk, and business value.
    • Lead a small engineering/platform team responsible for enterprise AI solutions, integrations, administration, and support.
    • Partner with business leaders to drive responsible adoption and measurable productivity improvement from enterprise AI.

Education & Licensing

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Artificial Intelligence or a related field from an accredited college or university required. Masters Degree preferred.

    • 10+ years of engineering, platform, or enterprise technology experience with 5+ years in technical leadership.
    • Strong hands-on understanding of LLMs, agentic AI, RAG, APIs, workflow automation, and enterprise integration.
    • Experience building AI solutions for corporate functions such as HR, Marketing, Finance, or Legal.

As an interpreter, you will receive training that is the best in the industry. We’ll ensure that you learn new skills while further developing your skillset. We provide numerous opportunities for advancement. You’ll be in a certified ASTM and ISO environment. You'll also be supported by a Senior Language Specialist, as well as our Interpreter and Technology Help Desks.

Join our team now!

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Marka-English Phone Interpreter

Job Title: Marka Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Phone Interpreter

Status: Independent Contractor

Pay: $0.75 - $0.90 per minute.

We Offer:

  • Employee Referral Program.
  • Advancement opportunities within the organization.
  • Interpreter support.
  • An inclusive and diverse work environment.
  • **This is an independent contractor position and therefore not eligible for employee benefits.**

Position Overview:

The Marka Telephone Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Markaand English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.

The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.

This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The Interpreters translate verbally.

**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment.**

Essential Job Functions

  • Respond to the interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

Qualifications

  • Fluency inMarkaand English and skilled in the associated cultural dynamics.
  • Ability to provide cultural competency and assess regional and accent differences to find ways of communicating with the LEP.
  • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.
  • Ability to concentrate, stay detached from the conversation, remain neutral and objective at all times, and remain on calls that involve sensitive subjects such as end of life conversations, pregnancy termination, vaccinations, and matters concerning sexual orientation and/or gender expression.
  • Education or work experience in language-related fields such as teaching, language assessment, translation or interpretation preferred.
  • Must be able to adapt to any LLS technology enhancements that improve service delivery and meet client demands.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States
  • Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with LanguageLine Solutions (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status).
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Candidates who are currently employed by a client of LanguageLine Solutions or an affiliated LanguageLine Solutions business may not be eligible for consideration.
  • Ability to read and write the requested languages - highly preferred.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**

Valsea - Where Innovation Meets Entertainment

At Valsea, we’re shaping the future of entertainment with immersive, engaging experiences that captivate players worldwide. Based in sunny Marbella, Spain, our vibrant open-space office is home to an international team of developers, marketers, product owners, and much more.

Valsea operates a leading scalable technology platform, 100% owned by us. This gives us the freedom to deliver results fast. We integrate selected outside companies into our ecosystem to ensure we provide fresh and vibrant products for our customers.

We work in a fast-paced environment, creating new brands, maintaining and improving our tech stack, launching leading acquisition and retention campaigns, and developing fresh features. Our ethos is simple - be best-in-class in everything we do.

Despite our rapid growth, Valsea still has that exciting start-up feel. We embrace a hybrid working model to balance professional growth with personal well-being. With a dynamic work environment, attractive salary, and a culture that thrives on collaboration, our power is our people.

We provide company laptops and other things you may need to work comfortably. Remote workers are always invited to our annual company trip and other team events. Ready to be part of something exciting?

What are we looking for now?

A Staff-level engineer who has done this before: someone who can walk into a mature, high-scale platform, understand where AI genuinely moves the needle versus where it's just noise, and lead the engineering work to get it done. You're comfortable being the most senior technical voice in the room, but you'd rather be pairing with an engineer on a gnarly integration than sitting in a strategy deck all day. You think in systems, not scripts: production reliability, data quality, and security aren't afterthoughts to you, they're the job.

This isn't a research role. It's a build role, with the freedom and seniority to also set direction.

What You'll do:

  • Own the technical strategy and roadmap for AI adoption across Valsea's product, platform, and internal tooling, grounded in what's actually feasible on our stack, not slideware.

  • Architect and lead the delivery of AI-powered capabilities into our Scala/Go/Kafka backend, from recommendation and personalisation to support/fraud/risk signals, agentic automation, and internal developer tooling.

  • Set the vision and roadmap for agentic QA automation (using AI agents to expand test coverage, catch regressions earlier, and reduce manual QA load) and for AI-accelerated support and incident response that cuts time-to-detect and time-to-resolve.

  • Introduce AI tooling at the root of our SDLC pipelines (GitHub/GitLab: code review, testing, deployment gates), so AI assistance is built into how the team ships, not bolted on afterward.

  • Evaluate and integrate LLM and ML infrastructure (self-hosted and API-based), making pragmatic build-vs-buy calls that respect our scale, latency, and cost constraints.

  • Set Product Development standards for how AI features get designed, tested, monitored, and rolled back. Model-driven systems should meet the same rigour as any other production service.

  • Partner directly with Engineering leadership, Product, and Data to identify where AI creates real player or business value, and turn that into a delivery plan.

  • Act as a technical multiplier: mentor senior and mid-level engineers and managers, run design reviews, and raise the technical bar for how the wider team thinks about AI-assisted and AI-driven systems.

  • Stay hands-on: prototype fast, get into the codebase, and unblock hard integration and performance problems yourself when it matters.

What You'll bring:

Who you are.

You're driven by purpose and curious by nature. You take ownership, speak up, and stay steady when things get hard. You'd rather the team win than get the credit. If that sounds like you, keep reading.

About the role.

The Senior Clinical Trial Manager will lead day-to-day clinical trial operations for assigned early-phase studies of our gene-editing therapeutics in rare genetic diseases. Reporting to the Senior Director of Clinical Operations, this role will be responsible for study execution from start-up through close-out, including site oversight, CRO and vendor management, trial documentation, timelines, budgets, and operational issue resolution.

In our lean biotech environment, this role requires a hands-on clinical operations leader who can manage multiple aspects of trial execution while partnering closely with internal teams, investigative sites, CROs, laboratories, and external vendors.

What you'll do.

  • Lead day-to-day clinical trial operations across assigned studies, sites, CROs, laboratories, and vendors.
  • Manage study start-up, site activation, monitoring oversight, and close-out activities.
  • Own and manage study timelines, budgets, invoices, vendor deliverables, and key milestones.
  • Oversee study documentation and trial master file quality to support inspection readiness.
  • Review and provide operational leadership on clinical documents, including protocols, ICFs, CRFs, SAPs, CSRs, study plans, and related materials.
  • Partner with cross-functional study teams to drive study execution, resolve operational issues, and support achievement of study milestones.
  • Manage clinical sample logistics between patients, sites, and laboratory vendors.
  • Drive timelines and logistics for Safety Review Boards, Data Monitoring Committees, data cuts, and related study activities.
  • Lead or support vendor review, selection, contracting, onboarding, and performance oversight.
  • Build and manage effective relationships with investigative sites, CROs, vendors, clinical experts, and internal stakeholders, including planning investigator meetings.
  • Identify, escalate, and resolve study risks and operational issues.
  • Represent the company externally with study partners and investigative sites.
  • Travel domestically and internationally to investigative sites or study-related meetings as needed.

What you bring.

  • Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, health-related, or related field.
  • 6+ years of progressive clinical operations experience in the pharmaceutical and/or biotechnology industry, including experience managing clinical trial execution from start-up through close-out.
  • Experience managing early-phase clinical studies; rare disease or CNS experience preferred.
  • Experience managing U.S. and global clinical trials across CROs, vendors, laboratories, and study sites.
  • Familiarity with ethics committee and regulatory submissions, such as pre-IND, IND, Scientific Advice, CTA, or similar filings.
  • Strong knowledge of GCP, ICH guidelines, clinical research regulations, and the drug development process.
  • Experience with vendor oversight, budgets, contracts, invoices, and change orders.
  • Strong clinical operations leadership, project coordination, planning, and organizational skills.
  • Proficiency with Smartsheet, Microsoft Office, or similar project and study tracking tools.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Knowledge of mRNA, RNAi, gene therapy, or gene-editing therapeutics; familiarity with LNP or AAV-based development preferred.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Hands-on mindset and willingness to work across multiple areas of clinical operations in a startup environment.

·Fully remote role

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Bilbao, Spain
jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Spain Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-110,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Description

Fetcherr builds responsible AI that transforms market complexity into measurable profit growth. At the core of the company is the Market Model - a proprietary AI-powered model delivering accurate, granular demand predictions with 96% forecast accuracy and real-time decision intelligence for commercial teams. Built on a glass-box architecture, it uses market data - not personal data - with full transparency into logic and outcomes. First deployed in global aviation, the technology is industry-agnostic and scales across volatile markets. Fetcherr delivers a consistent average profit uplift of 7%, with corporate partners including Delta, Virgin Atlantic, WestJet, Viva, and Azul. While Fetcherr initially focused on the airline industry, the company is now expanding into additional verticals, bringing its dynamic AI-driven optimization capabilities to new industries such as travel, mobility, retail, e-commerce, and beyond.

Having successfully transformed airline pricing, Fetcherr is now expanding into the ferry industry, bringing AI-driven revenue optimization to leading ferry operators.

We are looking for a Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support the development of an AI-driven pricing solution tailored to ferry operations. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience in ferry revenue management, route and sailing pricing, mixed passenger/vehicle/freight inventory optimization, or demand forecasting within a large-scale ferry operator. This role serves as a strategic advisor to our Product, Data Science, Engineering, and Customer teams, helping shape our ferry solution, validate business assumptions, and guide product and data strategy.

Responsibilities

Industry Leadership

  • Serve as Fetcherr's primary authority on ferry revenue management, pricing, demand forecasting, and commercial operations, advising Product, Engineering, Data Science, Solutions, and Commercial teams.
  • Provide expertise on ferry pricing dynamics, including:
  • Route, sailing, and one-way vs. return pricing
  • Accommodation category management (cabins, reclining seats, deck, pet cabins)
  • Vehicle pricing across cars, motorhomes, motorcycles, and trailers
  • Ro-ro freight pricing — accompanied vs. unaccompanied units, contracted vs. spot rates
  • Promotions, early booking, last-minute and walk-up pricing
  • Group bookings, tour operator allotments, and coach traffic
  • Resident fares, public service obligation (PSO) and territorial continuity routes, and other regulated fare regimes
  • Guide revenue management strategies balancing passenger load, vehicle deck and lane-meter yield, accommodation occupancy, and profitability across seasonal fleet deployments.
  • Advise on ancillary revenue optimization — accommodation upgrades, priority boarding, onboard dining, lounges, Wi-Fi, pet accommodation, and flexible-fare products — and on dynamic pricing across the short booking curve and high walk-up share characteristic of ferry demand.

Data & Product Development

  • Own the definition of ferry operational data requirements: reservations, passenger and vehicle manifests, accommodation and deck inventory, lane-meter utilization, route and sailing performance, cancellations and no-shows, onboard purchases, freight contracts, pricing, and promotional campaigns.
  • Lead discovery workshops and data mapping sessions, and translate ferry business processes into product requirements and AI modeling logic.
  • Define business rules, operational constraints, and regulatory fare obligations, and ensure they are correctly represented in the pricing engine.
  • Review and validate model assumptions and pricing outputs against real-world ferry scenarios.
  • Support development of scalable data ingestion and modeling processes.

Customer & Commercial Engagement

THE TEAM

The Underwriting Account Executive leads the execution and servicing of assigned accounts, coordinating internal and external stakeholders to support successful placement, retention, and growth. This role manages the full account lifecycle—from submission through binding and renewal—while ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and alignment with client and carrier requirements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Followingis a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.

  • Manage accounts from submission through binding, including coordinating all required documentation and communications

  • Partner with brokers and underwriters tosolicit, quote, andmaintainnew and renewal business

  • Negotiate coverage terms with carriers, including pricing, deductibles, enhancements, and exclusions

  • Selectappropriate carriersand manage the marketing process for assigned accounts

  • Prepare and deliver quotes, coverage comparisons, and recommendations to support placement decisions

  • Process new business, renewals, endorsements, and cancellations, ensuring accuracy and compliance with internal and carrier guidelines

  • Issue binders, invoices, and confirm coverage details, ensuring all documentation is complete andaccurate

  • Maintain ongoing communication with agents, carriers, and internal stakeholders to ensuretimelyexecution of account activities

  • Support retention and renewal strategies byidentifyingopportunities to expand coverage and strengthen client relationships

  • Provide guidance and direction to support staff as needed to ensure efficient workflow and service delivery

  • Conduct research and prepare account or market analysis to support client and business development efforts

  • Maintainaccuraterecords and manage all correspondencein accordance withcompany standards

  • Stay current on industry trends, market conditions, and carrier capabilities through ongoing education and training

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge,skilland/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience

  • Progressive experience in wholesale insurance, brokerage, or underwriting support roles (typically 3+ years)

  • Demonstrated experience managing accounts, marketing business, and supporting placement activities

  • Strong understanding of insurance products, coverage structures, and market dynamics

  • Ability to independently manage multiple priorities and make informed decisions with limited supervision

CERTIFICATIONS, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • Active state insurance licenserequiredin applicable lines of business

FUNCTIONAL SKILLS

  • Strong knowledge of insurance products, underwriting processes, and carrier guidelines

  • Ability to negotiate terms and evaluate coverage options to supportoptimalplacement outcomes

  • Effective account management skills across the full lifecycle (submission, quoting, binding, renewal)

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability tointerface acrossinternal and external stakeholders

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and accuracy

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and adapt in a fast-paced environment

  • Proficiencyin Microsoft Office and systems used for policy and account management

  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build andmaintainrelationships with agents, carriers, and internal teams

  • Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment in decision-making

  • Commitment to continuous learning and staying current on industry trends and market developments

Job Posting Description

FIS is a global leader in financial technology, helping banks, capital markets firms and asset managers move money, unlock growth and deliver confidence. We power the world’s economy through innovation, scale and expertise—and we’re just getting started.


About the Team

This role sits within the Capital Markets Managed & Cloud Services Presales organization, a globally distributed team supporting over 100 financial services products across trading, risk, treasury, lending and asset services platforms.


What You Will Be Doing

This is an advanced professional role with broad understanding of managed cloud services and all its strengths to existing and prospective clients. You will need to be able to resolve complex issues requiring in-depth knowledge and skills around the product as well as operational processes related to FIS Capital Markets solutions.   • Excellent client-facing communication and stakeholder management
  • Ability to work well independently or in a team environment
  • Be based anywhere in the United State of America or Canada

Added bonus if you have:

– AWS or Azure certifications

  • Capital Markets or regulated industry experience

At FIS, you can learn, grow and make an impact in your career. Our benefits include:

SENIOR STRATEGIC HEALTHCARE PARTNER: Global Hospital & Biosimilars


ROLE PURPOSE:

The Senior Strategic Healthcare Partner (SSHP) is a strategic, non-demand-generating role that strengthens partnerships across the Ontario healthcare ecosystem in gastroenterology, rheumatology, and hospital/institutional care.


With a distinct, non-promotional mandate, the SSHP builds trusted relationships with healthcare professionals, institutions, hospital leaders, and community stakeholders to identify care gaps and co-create solutions that improve access, timeliness, care pathways, patient flow, system capacity, and sustainability.


The SSHP collaborates compliantly across functions, including field and Head Office partners, while preserving its non-promotional mandate. As a strategic bridge between Pfizer and healthcare stakeholders, the SSHP translates system insights and evolving healthcare and pharmacy practices into quality-improvement initiatives aligned with Global Hospital & Biosimilars priorities.


The role requires a creative, entrepreneurial, customer-centric, proactive leader who can navigate complex healthcare environments, build trusted partnerships, and mobilize stakeholders around innovative solutions that improve access and support a more efficient, sustainable healthcare system.


RESPONSIBILITIES:


Gastroenterology (IBD) / Rheumatology

  • Partner with community and academic gastroenterology and rheumatology stakeholders to understand patient journeys, care pathways, system readiness, unmet patient and healthcare-system needs, and barriers to timely, appropriate care.
  • Co-create scalable workflow and care-pathway solutions that improve patient flow, practice capacity, and care delivery.
  • Generate system insights that support efficient, sustainable, patient-centred care models.

Hospitals & Institutions

  • Serve as a strategic partner to hospitals and institutions, focusing on oncology biosimilars, supportive care, and anticoagulation.
  • Understand institutional care pathways, operational challenges, and system readiness.
  • Collaborate with institutional stakeholders to improve infusion capacity, patient flow, continuity of care, and, where appropriate, institution-led biosimilar transitions.
  • Co-create quality-improvement initiatives that optimize capacity, resources, and sustainability.
  • Build trusted relationships with pharmacy directors, clinic managers, medical leaders, and other key stakeholders.

Strategic Partnerships & Healthcare-System Innovation

  • Explore innovative partnership models, tools, workflows, and care-enablement approaches addressing identified patient and system needs.
  • Support standardized processes and frameworks aligned with Canadian evidence-based guidelines, expert opinion, and stakeholder needs.
  • Lead or support compliant Strategic Healthcare Enhancement Projects and quality-improvement initiatives with appropriate governance and defined responsibilities.
  • Generate and communicate healthcare-system insights to inform organizational understanding and strategic planning.
  • Support sharing and scaling relevant quality-improvement learnings across healthcare settings.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Compliance

  • Collaborate compliantly with cross-functional colleagues, with clear roles and responsibilities within each function’s scope.
  • Maintain the SSHP’s distinct, non-promotional, non-demand-generating mandate in all activities and engagements.
  • Represent Pfizer at relevant conferences, meetings, and events as a credible strategic partner.
  • Conduct all activities according to applicable Pfizer policies, procedures, non-promotional standards, and compliance requirements.
  • Identify and report adverse events and product complaints in accordance with Corporate requirements, including Your Reporting Responsibilities requirements.

What You Bring

  • University degree in Life Sciences, Health Sciences, Pharmacy, Business Administration, or a related field; an advanced degree is an asset.
  • 8+ years of relevant pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, or healthcare experience, including strategic partnership, institutional, field-based, or healthcare-system roles.
  • Experience in quality improvement, co-creation, system partnerships, and/or complex projects.
  • Strong understanding of the Canadian healthcare environment, patient pathways, and evolving healthcare and pharmacy models.
  • Strategic, creative, and entrepreneurial mindset, with the ability to translate complex healthcare needs into practical, scalable solutions.
  • Strong relationship-building and influencing skills, with credibility among senior healthcare stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and collaborate effectively and compliantly across functions.
  • Strong project management, strategic planning, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong initiative, adaptability, and comfort navigating complexity and ambiguity.
  • Experience in specialty care, biologics, biosimilars, gastroenterology, rheumatology, and/or hospital-based care is an asset.
  • Bilingualism is an asset.

Role Requirements

  • Field-based role; must reside in Ontario, preferably in the greater Toronto area.
  • Ability to travel regularly within the territory, nationally, and internationally as required.
  • Valid driver’s licence and driving record that meets applicable Pfizer requirements.
  • Maintain documentation required for international travel.

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $107,400 to $179,000.

The salary range provided applies to Canada only and does not apply to any other locations outside of Canada.


PARTENAIRE STRATÉGIQUE PRINCIPAL EN SANTÉ : Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires, Marché mondial


RAISON D’ÊTRE DU POSTE

Le Partenaire stratégique principal en santé (SSHP) joue un rôle stratégique, distinct des activités de génération de la demande, qui renforce les partenariats au sein du réseau de la santé de l'Ontario, notamment en gastroentérologie, en rhumatologie et dans les milieux hospitaliers et institutionnels.


Dans le cadre d’un mandat distinct et non promotionnel, la personne titulaire développe des relations de confiance avec les professionnels de la santé, les établissements, les dirigeants hospitaliers et les partenaires communautaires afin de cerner les lacunes et de cocréer des solutions améliorant l’accès, la rapidité de prise en charge, les trajectoires de soins, le cheminement des patients, la capacité du système et sa pérennité.


Dans ce rôle, la personne collabore avec les partenaires internes, sur le terrain et au siège social, dans le respect des exigences de conformité et de son mandat non promotionnel. Lien stratégique entre Pfizer et les acteurs du réseau, elle transforme les perspectives du terrain et l’évolution des pratiques en santé et en pharmacie en initiatives d’amélioration de la qualité alignées sur les priorités du secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires, Marché mondial.


La personne recherchée fait preuve de créativité, d’esprit entrepreneurial, de proactivité et d’une forte orientation partenaires. Elle sait évoluer dans des environnements complexes, bâtir des partenariats de confiance et mobiliser les parties prenantes autour de solutions novatrices améliorant l’accès aux soins et l’efficacité et la durabilité du système.


RESPONSABILITÉS


Gastroentérologie (MII) / Rhumatologie

  • Collaborer avec les intervenants en gastroentérologie et en rhumatologie des milieux communautaires et universitaires afin de comprendre le parcours des patients, les trajectoires de soins, l’état de préparation du système, les besoins non comblés et les obstacles à un accès approprié et rapide aux soins.
  • Cocréer des solutions évolutives pour les processus et trajectoires de soins afin d’améliorer le cheminement des patients, la capacité clinique et la prestation des soins.
  • Faire émerger des perspectives sur le réseau afin de soutenir des modèles de soins efficaces, durables et centrés sur le patient.

Hôpitaux et établissements de santé

  • Agir comme partenaire stratégique auprès des hôpitaux et établissements, particulièrement pour les biosimilaires en oncologie, les soins de soutien et l’anticoagulation.
  • Comprendre les trajectoires de soins en établissement, les enjeux opérationnels et l’état de préparation du système.
  • Collaborer avec les partenaires des établissements afin d’améliorer la capacité des services de perfusion, le cheminement des patients, la continuité des soins et, lorsque pertinent, les transitions vers les biosimilaires menées par les établissements.
  • Cocréer des initiatives d’amélioration de la qualité qui optimisent la capacité, les ressources et la pérennité du système.
  • Développer des relations de confiance avec les directions de pharmacie, les gestionnaires de cliniques, les responsables médicaux et autres parties prenantes clés.

Partenariats stratégiques et innovation dans le réseau de la santé

  • Explorer des modèles de partenariat, outils, processus et approches novatrices répondant aux besoins définis des patients et du réseau.
  • Soutenir des processus et cadres de travail standardisés, conformes aux lignes directrices canadiennes fondées sur les données probantes, aux avis d’experts et aux besoins des parties prenantes.
  • Diriger ou soutenir, conformément aux exigences, des projets stratégiques d’amélioration des soins et des initiatives d’amélioration de la qualité avec une gouvernance et des responsabilités définies.
  • Recueillir et communiquer des perspectives sur le réseau de la santé afin d’éclairer la compréhension organisationnelle et la planification stratégique.
  • Favoriser le partage et la mise à l’échelle des apprentissages pertinents en amélioration de la qualité dans différents milieux de soins.

Collaboration interfonctionnelle et conformité

  • Collaborer avec les collègues des différentes fonctions, dans le respect des exigences de conformité, avec des rôles et responsabilités clairement définis selon le champ d’activité de chaque fonction.
  • Préserver le mandat distinct, non promotionnel et non axé sur la génération de la demande du SSHP dans toutes les activités et interactions.
  • Représenter Pfizer lors de congrès, réunions et événements pertinents à titre de partenaire stratégique crédible.
  • Mener toutes les activités conformément aux politiques et procédures de Pfizer, aux normes non promotionnelles et aux exigences de conformité.
  • Identifier et signaler les événements indésirables et les plaintes relatives aux produits conformément aux exigences de l’entreprise, y compris celles liées aux responsabilités en matière de signalement.

PROFIL RECHERCHÉ

  • Diplôme universitaire en sciences de la vie, en sciences de la santé, en pharmacie, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe. Un diplôme d’études supérieures constitue un atout.
  • Au moins 8 ans d’expérience pertinente dans les secteurs pharmaceutique, biopharmaceutique ou des soins de santé, notamment dans des fonctions liées aux partenariats stratégiques, aux établissements de santé, au travail sur le terrain ou au réseau de la santé.
  • Expérience en amélioration de la qualité, cocréation, partenariats avec le réseau et/ou projets complexes.
  • Excellente compréhension du système de santé canadien, des trajectoires de soins des patients et de l’évolution des modèles de prestation des soins et des pratiques pharmaceutiques.
  • Esprit stratégique, créatif et entrepreneurial, avec la capacité de transformer des besoins complexes du réseau de la santé en solutions pratiques et évolutives.
  • Excellentes aptitudes relationnelles et d’influence, et crédibilité auprès des décideurs et parties prenantes de haut niveau.
  • Capacité démontrée à exercer un leadership d’influence et à collaborer efficacement avec différentes fonctions, dans le respect des exigences de conformité.
  • Excellentes compétences en gestion de projet, planification stratégique, communication et mobilisation des parties prenantes.
  • Grand sens de l’initiative, capacité d’adaptation et aisance dans la complexité et l’ambiguïté.
  • Une expérience dans les soins spécialisés, les médicaments biologiques, les biosimilaires, la gastroentérologie, la rhumatologie et/ou les soins hospitaliers constitue un atout.
  • Bilinguisme (français et anglais) – le ou la titulaire du poste doit pouvoir bien communiquer en anglais, car ses fonctions exigent des interactions avec des intervenants et collègues se trouvant à l’extérieur du Québec ou du Canada.

EXIGENCES DU POSTE

  • Poste sur le terrain. La personne retenue doit résider en Ontario, de préférence dans la grande région de Toronto.
  • Capacité à se déplacer régulièrement dans le territoire ainsi qu’à l’échelle nationale et internationale, selon les besoins.
  • Permis de conduire valide et dossier de conduite conforme aux exigences applicables de Pfizer.
  • Maintenir à jour les documents requis pour les déplacements internationaux.

Le salaire annuel de base pour ce poste varie de 107,400$ à 179,000$.

L’échelle salariale fournie s’applique seulement au Canada, et ne s’applique à aucun autre endroit à l’extérieur du Canada.

Veeva is building the industry cloud for Life Sciences through software, data, AI, and business consulting working together. Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website.

Consulting is changing, and we’re not like other firms. Launched in 2019, Veeva Business Consulting has grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep domain knowledge with innovative technology to help Life Sciences companies work in a more efficient and connected way.

We are growing aggressively as we look towards 2030. We are seeking great people to help shape the future of the industry with the world’s leading software, data, AI, and expertise at their back.

The Role

As a Consultant in our Commercial Business Consulting practice, you won’t just advise on the future of Life Sciences - you’ll be building it. We help our customers bring treatments to patients faster by fundamentally transforming their operating models, powered by the industry’s most advanced technology, AI and data. Unlike traditional firms, we move beyond "slides and theory" to deliver tangible, scalable execution that others simply cannot replicate.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead project workstreams from end-to-end, ensuring the high-quality design and delivery of customer solutions
  • Solve complex problems for Life Sciences leaders, leveraging Veeva’s unique data and software insights
  • Mentor and manage Associate Consultants, overseeing their work and professional development within your workstream
  • Drive practice growth by contributing to business development and internal IP creation

Requirements

  • Experience: 3+ years in Life Sciences Consulting (Business or Management Consulting preferred)
  • Domain Knowledge: Proven expertise in one of: Go-to-Market strategy, Brand Planning, Product Launch, Omnichannel strategy, Segmentation and targeting
  • Analytical Rigor: A strong mindset for both quantitative and qualitative reasoning
  • Communication: Ability to articulate complex ideas clearly to senior stakeholders
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher
  • Not a perfect match yet? If you have 3–5 years of life sciences experience, a recent advanced degree, or a military background, Master Class is your pathway to a consulting career. [Explore Master Class]

Nice to Have

  • Knowledge of Veeva products
  • Experience delivering SaaS or Tech-enabled consulting solutions

Interviewing with Veeva

  • Follow the application process and submit your resume.
  • Within 3 days, you will receive a link to a personality assessment administered by a third party.
  • Once you complete the assessment, our team will review your full application package and follow up via email with our decision.
  • If moving to the interview stage, the process is as follows:
    1. A conversation with the hiring manager
    2. A practical case exercise
    3. A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader.
  • Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

  • Compensation: Highly competitive salary and equity in Veeva
  • Growth: Unrivalled career progression in a fast-growing, global team
  • Flexibility: Veeva is a Work Anywhere company. You can work from home or the office on any given day

Compensation

jobs.excerpt: We're growing, and we're looking for a Service Technician (we call the position Client Care Specialist) to join our team and own the client experience in the Central Georgia market.
jobs.description:
We're growing, and we're looking for a Service Technician (we call the position Client Care Specialist) to join our team and own the client experience in the Central Georgia market. If you're a self-driven AV pro who gets excited about solving problems, loves working with people, and doesn't need someone looking over your shoulder to get things done — keep reading.

Since we don't have an office in the area, your home will be your base of operations as you service AV clients in the central GA/Atlanta area, preferably in the South Atlanta to Macon corridor. You’ll have a company vehicle for client site visits and the full support of our Client Care team behind you.

Who We Are

S&L Integrated is a commercial Audio/Video/Controls/Lighting integration company based in in Thomasville, GA and Nashville, TN. We design, install, and support AV systems for commercial clients across the Southeast — and we take a lot of pride in doing it well. Our team is tight-knit, passionate about technology, and genuinely committed to making our clients' lives easier.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Being the go-to person for your assigned commercial AV clients — the one they trust to pick up the phone and actually fix things
  • Troubleshooting and resolving AV system issues — remotely when possible, on-site when needed
  • Keeping a close eye on client systems through remote monitoring tools and staying ahead of problems before clients even notice them
  • Keeping accurate client service documentation that is submitted timely
  • Making sure every client interaction reflects the level of service S&L is known for
  • Staying sharp — we invest in our people, and we expect you to keep learning alongside us

The Schedule

You will typically work a standard 40-hour work week, Monday–Friday. On-site visits can occasionally run long, so there may be periodic overtime.

What You Bring to the Table

Must-Haves:

  • Real-world experience in AV installation and/or AV service and troubleshooting for a commercial AV integration company.

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Chennai, India
jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.excerpt: At SPD Technology, we bring together a team of like-minded people who are driven by the desire to bring value through their work, united in their commitment to high performance and delivering custom, cutting-edge tech solutions that drive clients' growth.
jobs.description:
At SPD Technology, we bring together a team of like-minded people who are driven by the desire to bring value through their work, united in their commitment to high performance and delivering custom, cutting-edge tech solutions that drive clients' growth. We empower our people with a culture of excellence, and enable them with the opportunity to uphold their accountability to contribute on each level. We value humanity and collaboration, encourage professional and personal growth, and foster a supportive and flexible work environment where everyone's contribution is welcomed.

We are looking for Senior Payments Processing Engineer to join us as part of our team

About the role

As a Senior Payments Processing Engineer you will join a product team building payment infrastructure for merchants and partner platforms. The platform enables businesses to accept payments, manage payouts, process card and bank transactions, and handle payment-related operations without relying on multiple disconnected providers.

The engineering challenges go far beyond basic payment integrations. The platform handles payment orchestration, transaction processing, settlement and reconciliation, payouts, fraud and KYC integrations, and complex failure scenarios across systems that the team does not fully control.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who understands how money actually moves through payment systems and is comfortable owning critical backend flows end to end.

Tech Stack

  • TypeScript across the board, in a pnpm monorepo
  • NestJS backend services; Next.js and React on the front end
  • PostgreSQL, with SQL-first data modeling and versioned migrations
  • Event-driven service orchestration, webhooks, and idempotent processing
  • Acquirer and vendor integrations for card/ACH acceptance, fraud screening, payouts, and KYC
  • Managed cloud infrastructure, containerized services, CI/CD on GitHub
  • AI-assisted development as a standard part of the toolchain, not a side experiment

Work environment

Full-time, remote. Daily collaboration with a US-based team (4–6 hours of overlap with US Central Time is required)

As a qualified expert You will

  • Own end-to-end payment flows in TypeScript/NestJS services: authorization, capture, void, refund, dispute handling, and payout initiation and confirmation.
  • Build and maintain acquirer and processor integrations, keeping the platform acquirer-agnostic behind clean internal abstractions.
  • Design embedded and hosted checkout experiences (hosted fields, iframes, tokenization) that keep sensitive cardholder and bank data out of internal systems and minimize PCI scope.
  • Implement fee calculation and rate logic, including tiers, interchange-plus, flat structures, rounding rules, special rates, and edge cases.
  • Build the reconciliation and settlement layer to match processor reports and settlement files against internal records and surface breaks.
  • Design event handling incorporating idempotency keys, out-of-order and duplicate webhooks, retries with backoff, and state machines.
  • Integrate fraud, bank-account verification, and KYC providers, tuning decisioning against real outcomes.
  • Handle ACH mechanics including submission windows, returns, return codes, NOCs, and retry rules.
  • Ensure correctness in the domain, maintaining complete audit trails and producing reconciliation evidence.
  • Act as the team's payments expert, advising product on rail capabilities and reviewing payment-adjacent code.

What Success Looks Like

  • First 30 days — you can trace any transaction through the platform end to end, and you have documented the gaps and risks you see in current flows.
  • First 90 days — you own a critical payment domain including its specs, tests, and reconciliation checks, and you have shipped a meaningful improvement to reliability or correctness.
  • First 6 months — payment orchestration in your area is provably correct and observable, adding a new processor or payout rail is a well-understood exercise rather than an adventure, and you are the person the team and the business rely on for payments judgment.

We're looking for you if you have

  • 6+ years building production software, with at least 3 years hands-on in payments, and direct ownership of live payment flows.
  • Concrete experience integrating a payment processor, gateway, or acquirer (Adyen, Stripe, Braintree, Worldpay, Checkout.com, Fiserv, or similar) beyond a starter integration — including webhooks, reporting, and edge-case handling.
  • Practical understanding of the card lifecycle (auth, capture, settlement, refund, chargeback, representment) and of ACH/bank rails (NACHA basics, returns, timing).
  • Working knowledge of PCI DSS obligations and of the architectural patterns that reduce scope: tokenization, hosted fields, iframe isolation, and data-flow segregation.
  • Strong TypeScript/Node.js skills and solid relational data modeling — you can design a schema whose invariants make an inconsistent ledger structurally difficult.
  • A rigorous approach to reconciliation and idempotency, informed by having been on the hook when something didn't balance.
  • Fluency with modern AI-assisted development tooling, paired with the discipline to verify — in payments, plausible-looking code that is subtly wrong is the expensive kind.
  • Strong English communication skills and confidence working directly with a US-based team.
  • Ability to work with 4–6 hours of daily overlap with US Central Time.

Bonus points

  • Experience with platform, marketplace, or facilitator models (split payments, sub-merchant onboarding, multi-party flows).
  • Experience with payouts and disbursement rails, including bank-account collection, verification, and payout status handling.
  • Experience with fraud and risk tooling, and bank-account validation services.
  • Experience with e-commerce plugin or SDK development (WooCommerce, Shopify, Magento).
  • Knowledge of multi-currency, cross-border, or alternative payment methods.
  • Experience with event sourcing applied to financial state, and double-entry ledger design.

What's in it for You

Reveal great tech solutions

Join the team of experts who create custom, cutting-edge tech solutions for world-renowned businesses, fueling clients growth. Unleash your potential, tackle new challenges, and be part of a team that values your skills and contributions. Focus on long-term impact and building tailored, long-lasting partnerships with our clients.

Experience an agile and flexible working environment

Work fully remote around the globe, or in a hybrid work model from our office hubs which are equipped with everything needed for comfortable work. Enjoy a flexible working schedule and create work and rest balance for yourself. Empower yourself with a stable workload and a stable income, focusing on lasting cooperation and high-performance culture.

Embrace the opportunity for personal and professional growth

Take advantage of performance review and career path. Elevate your skills with mentorship program, personal development plan, and individual learnings through the corporate library, public speaking support, and more.

Feel cared about

Be among like-minded people and feel supported with collaboration, open communication and mutual respect. Join company-wide tech and cultural events, and contribute to meaningful CSR initiatives that resonate with your values.

Interview steps

  1. Interview with Recruiter
  2. Technical Interview
  3. Client Interview.

WHO WE ARE:

Splice is a creative platform for people who make music. Serious producers choose Splice Sounds to bring their ideas to life. A subscription to Splice inspires and accelerates creative success for digital music creators with an industry-leading catalog of sounds and samples and an expanding AI stack. Via Splice, an unparalleled team of sound designers and sample creators are fueling the success of a growing global community of chart-topping producers, students, and DIY creators.

HOW WE WORK:

At Splice, DISCO is a rallying cry for collaboration, accountability, and unity within our organization; Direct, Inclusive, Splice Together, Creator Centric, and Optimistic. Our shared success depends on our ability to support one another, work well together, and communicate directly. By embracing flexibility and a unified approach, we can navigate anything that’s thrown at us.

Splice embraces a culture of remote work. You’ll see your colleagues showing up from across the US and the UK. In order to keep us working well as a team, we have regular communication, including Town Halls, departmental all-hands and get-togethers.

When you join Splice, you join a network of colleagues, peers, and collaborators. Are you ready?

JOB TITLE: Senior Product Designer II
LOCATION: Remote, US only

THE ROLE
You know how to read a funnel, identify where an experience is failing, and fix it with the same craft and precision you'd bring to anything else. You bring a clear point of view to ambiguous work, hold craft standards even when things move fast, and design toward outcomes you can actually measure. You'll work closely with our Principal Designer on Growth across the full scope of how Splice acquires, activates, and retains creators.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Execute high-quality design across the full growth scope. Onboarding, subscription and paywall experiences, referral programs, core site, and lifecycle moments. You carry the craft standard across all of it, from early concept through shipped product.
  • Partner with our Principal Designer on Growth to shape what gets built. You bring a point of view early, share it clearly, and then hold it loosely enough to change your mind when the work proves you wrong. You contribute to product decisions, not just execute them. You push back if briefs are too vague and distill fuzzy input into clear design questions.
  • Drive experimentation with rigor. You identify where experience and data signal a real problem, frame a hypothesis, design the variants, and interpret results to inform what comes next. You know what a good experiment looks like and what makes a bad one — including when they’re scoped too small to tell you anything, aimed at the wrong lever, or when the result is actually pointing you at the real problem elsewhere entirely.
  • Ship work that moves metrics. Success is concrete: more creators completing onboarding, stronger conversion through the subscription experience, lifecycle moments that bring people back. You'll see the numbers and know which ones you moved.
  • Collaborate closely with Marketing, PMs, engineers, and data scientists. You build working relationships that make fast, high-quality shipping possible. You communicate trade-offs clearly and keep things moving without waiting on a handoff.
  • Contribute to the design system. You build in a way that scales, flag inconsistencies when you see them, and contribute components when you identify gaps.
  • Use AI-native tools as a standard part of your practice. Cursor, Claude, and similar tools belong in your daily workflow — for rapid prototyping, exploring directions, and accelerating execution.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

  • 7+ years of product design experience, with meaningful time in a growth, conversion, or retention context. You've shipped real work that produced real outcomes.
  • Your portfolio shows a refined eye and a high standard of execution. Work that doesn't demonstrate this clearly won't move forward.
  • You are already using AI-native tools (Cursor, Claude, or equivalent) as a standard part of your workflow. This is a baseline expectation, not a bonus.
  • Experimentation fluency. You understand A/B testing, how to design for it, and how to read results without over-indexing on noise.
  • Funnel thinking. You can map a conversion funnel, identify where experience quality and business outcomes diverge, and design toward a specific outcome without losing sight of the user.
  • Metric fluency. You know which metrics matter for growth, how to interpret them in context, and how to set up a design decision so it can actually be measured.
  • You work fluidly within established design systems and contribute back to them.
  • You partner naturally with PMs and engineers. You influence product direction through your work and your thinking, not just your pixels.
  • You can present work clearly at every stage, from rough concept to leadership review, and articulate the reasoning behind a design decision without a lengthy preamble.

NICE TO HAVES

  • A genuine connection to music and creator culture. You understand what it means to be mid-session, chasing a sound, making something.
  • Front-end fluency (HTML/CSS/React). You can read and write code when it helps you move faster or communicate more precisely.
  • Experience with subscription or marketplace business models.

  • Time Off: Unlimited PTO to recharge and thrive.
  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with immediate vesting and company match.

  • Flexible Work Options: Work remotely or connect at our office hubs and creative spaces worldwide.
  • Professional Growth: Annual learning budget, leadership programs, and team ambassador opportunities.

Benefits

  • Ungedeckelte monatliche Provisionen auf jeden deiner Abschlüsse – ausgezahlt im Folgemonat

Du willst Vertrieb mit Substanz, echte Umsatzverantwortung und eine Mission, hinter der du stehen kannst?
